question: Primaquine, used for radical cure of Plasmodium vivax malaria (to eliminate hepatic hypnozoites), must be preceded by G6PD testing because it can cause life-threatening haemolytic anaemia in G6PD-deficient individuals.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Reconsider. Primaquine-induced haemolytic anaemia in G6PD deficiency can be severe and even fatal. G6PD testing before prescribing is a non-negotiable safety step in all P. vivax treatment guidelines.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Primaquine generates reactive oxygen species during metabolism. In G6PD-deficient red cells (unable to regenerate NADPH), this causes oxidative haemolysis. G6PD testing is mandatory before primaquine is prescribed.
